newsitem.title: USA: Clinton raised more money than needed - Gephardt.
newsitem.headline: Clinton raised more money than needed - Gephardt.

text.p: President Clinton did not have to raise as much money as he did to win a second term, Richard Gephardt, the House minority leader and a possible presidential contender in 2000, said Tuesday.
"President Clinton would have won this election without spending as much as was spent. That's my opinion. I may be wrong," the Missouri Democrat told a news conference at the Iowa statehouse.
"He ran a good campaign. People were pleased with his service as president and I think he would have won in any event," he said.

Gephardt refused to be drawn into the issue of whether Clinton focused too heavily on fundraising, a hot topic in Washington amid disclosures of White House coffees and overnight stays in the Lincoln bedroom for campaign givers.
"I have never seen a sitting president spend as much time talking to citizens than this president has. He works harder than anybody I've ever seen," Gephardt said.

He was in Iowa to meet privately with local Democrats considering runs for Congress next year. He denied the visit was a sign of his own presidential aspirations although Iowa frequently attracts potential candidates because it holds the initial contest of the presidential primary season.
Gephardt won Iowa's 1988 Democratic caucuses in his abbreviated run for the White House.
"We've got some very, very important issues in front of us right now and the last thing we need to be doing is to be talking about political races way out in the future," he said.

He also urged that changes be made in campaign finance laws before the next presidential campaign. "I hope it will be improved. I hope we get rid of soft money. I hope we give candidates free TV time," he said, referring to unlimited contributions permitted to the political parties and a Clinton-supported proposal to give candidates free time slots on television.
